info.text:
In 2023, US property and casualty insurers lost about $21 billion on underwriting yet earned $35.7 billion in net income, according to Verisk and the APCIA. This video explains the two ways insurers make money, underwriting and investing the float, and the combined ratio that grades them, with a worked example and the industry's ratios from 2020 to 2025. We open Progressive's 2025 10-K, show how higher interest rates lifted investment income, and cover catastrophe years, reinsurance, and what it all means for the people paying premiums.

Sources: Verisk/APCIA full-year 2025 report (Mar 25, 2026), first-half 2026 report (Sept 2, 2026) and 2021-2023 annual reports; AM Best First Look 2025 (Mar 23, 2026) and 2023 investment income report (May 28, 2024); Progressive Form 10-K FY2025 and December 2025 results release (Jan 28, 2026); Verisk LA wildfire estimate (Jan 22, 2025); ISO/PCI 2017 results (May 2018); Howden Re January 2026 renewal report; Federal Reserve FOMC statements (2022-2024).

News and education, not financial advice.
